summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, later teaching numerous disciples, including Ngulchu Yangchen Drubpai Dorje.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She pursued her PhD at Punjabi University, supervised by Inder Mohan Singh, and studied under the traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).
Nguyen Thi Xinh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University under the doctoral supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his MA at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

Nguyễn Ngọc Ánh specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned degrees from VNU-HCM University (BA 2011–2015), University of Delhi (MA 2016–2018), and University of Economics and Law (LLB 2021–2023), and was a PhD scholar at the University of Colombo in 2020.
Nhu Lien specializes in Buddhist studies, having studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.
Nhung Lu Rots specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied as a Stipendiat at the University of Oslo (attested 2026), where she was appointed a Postdoctoral Researcher in 2026.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology and with teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Gongga Rinpoche, and Hsu Yun. In Buddhist studies, he headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station and became a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (~1953).

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who founded Nipponzan-Myohoji. He studied at Rissho University (1912), Taisho University, Koyasan University, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji, and taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

Nicholas Dirks is a historian and Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). He held faculty posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) specialized in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Oxford under Rodney Needham, later lecturing at Durham (1972–1976) and serving as Reader in the Social Anthropology of South Asia at Oxford and Wolfson College.

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) was a linguist, Tibetologist, and Central Asian specialist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, where he taught (1923, 1925–1941), led Mongolian studies at the Institute of Oriental Studies, and was Professor of Mongolian at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) worked in history, archaeology, Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts, and founded the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute.

Nicholas Thanissaro works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a BSc from the University of Manchester (1985), a PGCE from Manchester Metropolitan University (1986), a PhD from the University of Warwick (2016), and an MA from the University of South Wales (2017).

Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from Stanford University (-2015). He held a JSPS postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Tokyo (2015–2017) and assistant professorships at Nanyang Technological University (2018) and the University of San Diego (2022).
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicol Macnicol (1870–1952) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his MA (~1887–1891) and D.Litt. (-1901) from the University of Glasgow and served as a missionary at Wilson College, Mumbai, beginning in 1895.
Nicola Bajetta is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he conducted doctoral research and served as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg.

Nicola Di Cosmo is a historian of Sinology and Central Asia. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (~1987–1991) and held appointments at Cambridge, Harvard, Canterbury, Columbia, and the Institute for Advanced Study as Henry Luce Foundation Professor (~2003).
